records.design: Prospective multicentre observational study during in-hospital resuscitation
records.scope_note: 567 cardiac arrests; 53 survivors and 28 interviews. Eleven interviewees reported memories or perceptions; none identified the visual target and one identified the auditory stimulus.
records.limitations: Survivor selection, low interview numbers and uncertain timing constrain interpretation. EEG during CPR does not establish that a recalled experience occurred during absent brain activity or irreversible death.
records.bq_contribution: Extends the existing resuscitation comparison without resolving survival beyond death.
records.verification_depth: Crossref, Europe PMC indexed author abstract and existing BQ001 record checked; full methods and EEG adjudication remain pending.

records.design: Four-laboratory proof-of-concept study of communication during REM sleep
records.scope_note: 36 participants; 29 correct responses across six people. Of 158 attempts during signal-verified lucid dreams, 18.4% were correct and 60.1% received no response.
records.limitations: Selected lucid-dream conditions, differing protocols and many non-responses limit generalisation. Ordinary sensory cues were used; this is not evidence of telepathy.
records.bq_contribution: Offers a way to probe reported awareness and simple cognition during dreams without relying entirely on later recall.
records.verification_depth: Crossref, Europe PMC and primary full-text methods/results inspected; no raw-data or independent replication appraisal.

records.design: High-density EEG with serial awakenings during REM and NREM sleep
records.scope_note: Posterior EEG activity was associated with subsequent reports of dreaming and aspects of reported content.
records.limitations: Correlates of a later report may partly reflect memory or reporting rather than experience itself. The EEG claim has been challenged; neither association nor prediction establishes a complete mechanism.
records.bq_contribution: Pairs a positive neural-correlate proposal with a blinded challenge and a methodological commentary.
records.verification_depth: Crossref and indexed author abstract checked. Primary full-text retrieval failed; sample appraisal remains pending. Ruby commentary inspected separately.

records.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials with active controls
records.scope_note: 47 trials and 3,515 participants. The review reported small to moderate improvements in some negative stress outcomes; findings varied by outcome and comparator.
records.limitations: Searches ended in November 2012. No demonstrated superiority to other active treatments is not proof of equivalence. This clinical review cannot establish societal flourishing or a metaphysical account of suffering.
records.bq_contribution: Supplies a bounded intervention-outcome reference for reducing suffering, with attention and wellbeing questions kept distinct.
records.verification_depth: Crossref and journal-record author abstract checked. The related AHRQ report has different trial totals and is not merged as an independent study; full-text appraisal pending.

records.design: Randomised compassion versus reappraisal training study
records.scope_note: Two weeks of training; 56 completed the protocol and 41 were analysed after excluding those who disbelieved the economic game. Compassion trainees redistributed more money than reappraisal trainees.
records.limitations: Selected analysis sample, short follow-up and a laboratory game limit generalisation to enduring real-world conduct. Neural associations do not establish a cosmic mechanism.
records.bq_contribution: Reuses the existing discovery lead to compare trainable compassion with behavioural outcomes and later, more cautious review evidence.
records.verification_depth: Crossref, Europe PMC and primary full-text methods/results inspected; supplements and independent replication remain pending.

records.design: Cross-sectional online survey of regular meditators
records.scope_note: 315 of 1,232 respondents (25.6%) recalled a particularly unpleasant experience they attributed to meditation.
records.limitations: Self-selection, recall and one broad question preclude a causal incidence estimate. Severity, duration and impairment were not characterised; unpleasant experiences are not interchangeable with lasting harm.
records.bq_contribution: Adds adverse-experience measurement to attention and wellbeing pathways rather than presenting contemplative practice as uniformly beneficial.
records.verification_depth: Crossref, Europe PMC and primary full-text limitations inspected; no longitudinal causal or clinical appraisal.

records.design: Blinded EEG classification challenge with separate data and analysis teams
records.scope_note: 54 one-minute NREM recordings from nine participants. Across five stages of progressively reduced blinding, classification did not perform significantly above chance.
records.limitations: Small sample and specific spectral-power features limit the result. It challenges this detection approach, not every possible neural marker of dreaming; it is not an identical replication of Siclari et al.
records.bq_contribution: Makes the disagreement about identifying dream experience from brain signals explicit alongside the positive study.
records.verification_depth: Crossref and Europe PMC indexed author abstract checked; full analytic pipeline and reanalysis remain pending.
